key_insight: KernelSeek steers GPU kernel optimization with timely questions rather than more tools or fixed recipes, helping a general-purpose coding agent challenge bottlenecks and explore new optimization paths.
engineering_relevance: Question-driven guidance could help engineers optimize CUDA kernels without operator-specific agent knowledge or a faster implementation to imitate.
method: Pair a general-purpose coding agent with a minimal harness enforcing a verifiable optimization goal.
Ask questions at decision points, initially from a human and later from a self-applied question bank.
Redirect attention across system layers and challenge claimed performance limits without prescribing implementations.
evidence_signal: The reported dependency-free attention forward kernels passed all 182 scenarios per architecture and achieved geometric-mean speedups of 1.16× over FlashAttention-3 on Hopper and 1.46× over FlashAttention-4 on Blackwell.
watch_item: The workflow initially relied on human questions, and the abstract does not establish how well fully autonomous questioning generalizes beyond attention kernels.
paper_title: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization
